A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPMA research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original PPMA classification, detection and segmentation results, together with mask ablations, throughput measurements and attention visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds COCO results under a longer training schedule and additional quantitative mask comparisons.

M1.justification: The polyline mask, horizontal and vertical decay factors, attention integrations and PPMA-T/S/B architectures remain unchanged. Linear-attention applications and the 3D extension were already present in v1's appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K classification, COCO2017 object detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20K semantic segmentation. The added COCO training schedule changes procedures within existing coverage; no new dataset or evaluated task is introduced.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 adds the Hilbert scan mask to the quantitative ablation comparison; v1 only visualized it. NAT-S also enters the COCO comparison in the new 3x block of Table 2, having previously appeared on other benchmarks.

E3.justification: V1 evaluates COCO with a 12-epoch 1x schedule. V2 retains this and adds 36-epoch, multi-scale 3x training in Section 5.2 and Table 2. Table 4 also adds throughput to the mask-ablation evaluation; existing ImageNet and ADE20K settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative Hilbert-mask testing and throughput comparisons across mask variants, extending the accuracy-versus-efficiency analysis. The shared-versus-separate decay-factor ablation and attention visualizations already existed in v1's appendix and are partly moved into the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged. New COCO 3x results report PPMA-B at 52.6 box AP and 46.3 mask AP, versus RMT-B at 52.2 and 46.1; these use a new training schedule. Table 4 adds Hilbert results of 82.44% top-1 accuracy and 48.14% mIoU, plus additional throughput entries such as 1779 images/s without a mask.

T1.justification: The definitions, proofs, complexity derivations and 3D formulation are retained. Appendix Theorems 3–5 become Theorems 1–3, and Corollaries 3–4 become Corollaries 1–2; these numbering corrections do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a 2D polyline mask, efficient decomposition and integration with ViT attention, and competitive vision-benchmark performance. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving semantic continuity, object boundaries and separate directional decay factors already appear in v1's appendices. GPU-memory overhead, slower inference and proposed CUDA/Triton optimization are also retained. The new Limitations label reorganizes an existing qualification.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 adds brief configuration information for the new COCO experiment: 36 epochs with multi-scale inputs. Architecture details, other hyperparameters, throughput hardware and code-access information remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 still documents only the 1x COCO schedule.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Vicinity Vision Transformer, cited as reference 39 in v2, and sharpens the comparison between input-independent spatial masks and Mamba2's input-dependent mask. The broader research positioning remains unchanged; most reference changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and cross-reference edits, consolidates Appendix B.4's ablation discussion into Section 5.4, and updates author information, the conference header and acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains separate 1x and 3x blocks, while Table 4 consolidates existing ablations and adds a throughput column. V1's detailed appendix architecture diagram becomes v2 Figure 5 with revised styling, and v2 Figure 7 redisplays selected existing attention examples. Duplicate appendix displays are removed.

improvement.justification: The added COCO 3x comparison tests whether the advantage persists under longer multi-scale training, while the Hilbert comparison and per-mask throughput measurements strengthen assessment of the design and its speed costs. Moving existing architecture and ablation material into the main text improves accessibility. These are useful, limited gains; the method, theory and original benchmark findings remain unchanged.
